passage:
A train station placed a piano in the main hall. Anyone could play it, but after complaints, the station added rules: no playing before 9 a.m., no songs longer than five minutes during busy hours, and no blocking the path.
Some musicians were unhappy. They said rules limited creativity. Travelers said the rules made the space comfortable for everyone.
After a month, the piano stayed popular. More people played because the rules made expectations clear.
The station manager said public art needs public responsibility. A shared space is not the same as a private stage.
Freedom works better when it considers the people who must share the room.
